record.original_question: Let f(x) be a polynomial in C[x] with exactly k monomials. Does there exist a number N(k) such that if the first N(k) moments M_n = integral_0^1 f(x)^n dx vanish for 1 <= n <= N(k), then f must be zero; and if such a number exists, determine N(k) or give a good upper bound for it.

evidence.quote: Problem 27. (i) Let f(x) be a polynomial in C[x] with k monomials. Is there a value N(k) such that if the following finite set of moment conditions hold (...) then f = 0? (ii) If the answer is yes, find N(k) or a good upper bound of this number.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k\ge 1$ be a positive integer and let $f(x)\in\mathbb{C}[x]$ be a polynomial having exactly $k$ monomials (i.e., $f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^k a_i x^{d_i}$ with nonzero coefficients $a_i\in\mathbb{C}$ and pairwise distinct nonnegative integer exponents $d_1<d_2<\cdots<d_k$). For each integer $n\ge 1$, define the $n$-th moment
$$M_n(f)\;=\;\int_0^1 f(x)^n\,dx.$$

(i) Does there exist a positive integer $N(k)$, depending only on $k$, such that whenever $f\in\mathbb{C}[x]$ has at most $k$ monomials and
$$M_n(f)=0\quad\text{for all }1\le n\le N(k),$$
one necessarily has $f\equiv 0$?

(ii) If such an $N(k)$ exists, determine its value, or give a sharp upper bound for $N(k)$ as a function of $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of finite moment determinacy for sparse (k-monomial) polynomials, in the form of finding a bound N(k) that forces vanishing of f from the first N(k) moments of f^n on [0,1], is discussed in work of Françoise–Pakovich–Yomdin–Zhao and related literature on the polynomial moment vanishing problem. While there are partial results (e.g., for small k and via composition conditions), no explicit finite N(k) bound for general k appears to be established, and the problem is treated as open.

status_evidence.title: Moment vanishing problem and positivity: Some examples
status_evidence.snippet: Examines the moment vanishing problem for sparse polynomials and discusses one-dimensional and multidimensional formulations without giving an explicit N(k).
status_evidence.claim: The finite-moment determinacy bound N(k) for k-monomial polynomials is treated as a problem of interest with only partial answers.

status_evidence.title: On decompositions of trigonometric polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Pakovich's work characterizes vanishing of moments via composition conditions for the polynomial moment problem.
status_evidence.claim: Moments-vanishing characterizations for polynomials are described via composition conditions, but a uniform N(k) bound is not given.
